review_comment:
I don't know how likely this scenario is but I suppose it's possible that after we set the `running` flag to false within the `AbstractProcessWorkerExecutorService` via the call to `shutdownNow`, an interrupt occurs while the service is completing the item it was running. In that situation I believe we won't call `notifyQueueRunnables()` because of the exception. What do you think about calling `priorityProcessWorker.notifyQueueRunnables()` before `killProcessIfPresent()` just in case? If the service already drained the queue then it shouldn't do anything.

I don't think it would hurt 🤔 

A side note, I wonder if `signalAndWaitForWorkerTermination` should call `shutdownNow()` 🤔

Good catch on the interrupt. 

I was worried about calling `notifyQueueRunnables()` while the executor is still running. I added a call to it if the `awaitTermination` returns success

Just curious, what's your concern about calling `notifyQueueRunnables()` while the executor is still running? I wonder if we should do the call right before the `killProcessIfPresent()` that way we handle the potential interrupt case here too.

Calling `notifyQueueRunnables()` was triggering the assertion here: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/dda08b3f3b749b440a0b9f50be58ec7e39594163/x-pack/plugin/ml/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/ml/job/process/AbstractProcessWorkerExecutorService.java#L141

I didn't want to remove that assertion
